previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a patient with stage IV cholangiocarcinoma, was admitted with recurrent fevers and found to have acute cholecystitis with a contained gallbladder rupture. He underwent percutaneous cholecystostomy tube placement, which drained purulent material. Post-procedure, he developed fevers, rigors, and a lactate of 5.5, consistent with severe sepsis, and was transferred to the ICU. Blood and gallbladder cultures confirmed E. coli infection, which showed intermediate sensitivity to meropenem. Antibiotics were switched to tigecycline, and a PICC line was placed for outpatient IV therapy. His condition improved with treatment, and he was discharged home to complete a 7-day course of tigecycline, with follow-up arranged for drain management and oncology care.

radiology_notes.text:
EXAMINATION:  CONTRAST ENHANCED CT ABDOMEN AND PELVIS

INDICATION:  Cholangiocarcinoma with biliary stents and recent gallbladder
rupture causing sepsis and requiring percutaneous cholecystostomy. Now
presenting with fevers and fatigue. Evaluate for cholangitis.

TECHNIQUE:  Axial MDCT images were obtained through the abdomen and pelvis
after the uneventful administration of IV contrast. No oral contrast was
provided. Sagittal and coronal reformats were generated.

TOTAL EXAM DLP: 682 MGy-cm.

COMPARISON:  Prior abdominal/ pelvic CT from ___.

FINDINGS: 

There is bibasilar linear atelectasis. No pleural or pericardial effusion
identified.
CT of the abdomen: There is redemonstration of a pigtail cholecystostomy tube
in the right upper quadrant, in unchanged position as compared to prior exam
from ___. Again the tube takes a transhepatic course and there is no
new fluid collection surrounding the tube or the gallbladder fossa.
Low-density material surrounding the gallbladder fossa is again seen, likley
inflammatory changes,  not significantly increased since prior. Fluid and
stranding along the colon has decreased since prior examination. There is no
new drainable collection seen within the liver. There is no subcapsular
hematoma. The portal vein is patent.
The patient has bilateral metallic biliary stents with 1 extending into the
left lobe of the liver. The right-sided stent again extends to the posterior
ducts on the right which are slightly more dilated as compared to prior. A
separate internal external drainage courses centrally via the left-sided stent
and again loops back on itself. There is expected pneumobilia, similar in
appearance to prior examination.
The adrenal glands and pancreas are normal. The spleen is enlarged measuring
15 cm. Note is made of accessory spleens. The left kidney contains a 10 mm
hypodensity at the lower pole, likely a cyst. The kidneys otherwise enhance
symmetrically and excrete contrast without evidence of hydronephrosis or renal
masses.
The stomach is collapsed. There is no small bowel obstruction. There are
sigmoid diverticula with no evidence of acute diverticulitis. The appendix is
not clearly visualized, however there is no evidence of acute appendicitis.
Small and large bowel are otherwise grossly unremarkable. There is no free
fluid. There is no free air.
CT of the pelvis: The urinary bladder and terminal ureters are normal. The
prostate is mildly enlarged. There is no pelvic free fluid. There is no
inguinal or pelvic lymph node enlargement by CT size criteria.
Osseous structures: No blastic or lytic lesion concerning for malignancy

IMPRESSION: 

1. No new fluid collection identified within the liver. Intrahepatic biliary
ducts are slightly more dilated on the right as compared to prior.
2. Unchanged positioning of biliary stents and internal-external biliary drain
which is coiled on itself in the distal end of the left metal stent.

NOTIFICATION:  Initial findings discussed with Dr. ___ In person at 340
AM. Discussed with ___ by NSR the telephone on ___ at
4:23AM.

EXAMINATION:  LIVER OR GALLBLADDER US (SINGLE ORGAN)

INDICATION:  ___ year old man with cholangiocarcinoma and multiple biliary
stents s/p ERCP  // assess for interval change in dilatation after ERCP

TECHNIQUE:  Grey scale and color Doppler ultrasound images of the abdomen were
obtained.

COMPARISON:  CT of the abdomen and pelvis dated ___.

FINDINGS: 

LIVER: The left lobe liver is not well evaluated due to obscuration by
overlying gas. Right lobe of the liver demonstrates normal echogenicity with
smooth contours. There is no ascites.

BILE DUCTS:  A percutaneous drain is partially visualized traversing the right
lobe of the liver. Left intrahepatic biliary ducts and common bile duct are
not visualized. There is mild prominence of the intrahepatic biliary ducts in
the right lobe, similar to comparison CT.

GALLBLADDER: The gallbladder is obscured by overlying gas.

PANCREAS: Visualized portions of the pancreatic head and body are within
normal limits without mass or pancreatic duct dilatation. The pancreatic tail
is obscured by overlying gas.

SPLEEN:  The spleen is enlarged, measuring 16.5 cm in length. A 1.6 cm
accessory spleen is incidentally noted near the tail of the pancreas.

IMPRESSION: 

1.  Poor visualization of left intrahepatic bile ducts due to overlying gas.
No evidence of increased biliary dilatation within the right hepatic lobe.
2.  Mild splenomegaly.

EXAMINATION:  CHEST PORT. LINE PLACEMENT

INDICATION:  ___ year old man with new picc  // L picc 50 cm ___ ___ 
Contact name: ___: ___     L picc 50 cm ___ ___

IMPRESSION: 

In comparison with the study of ___, there are lower lung volumes with
extensive atelectatic changes at the bases.  Otherwise, no change except for
placement of a left subclavian PICC line extends to the mid portion of the
SVC.

INDICATION:  ___ year old man with cholangiocarcinoma c/b GB rupture and GNR
sepsis, now s/p ERCP  // Eval for interval change s/p ERCP

TECHNIQUE:  The patient was brought to the fluoroscopy suite and placed supine
on the imaging table.  Scout radiographs of the abdomen were obtained before
this examination. Using sterile technique, the existing pigtail
cholecystostomy tube was on catheter and 25 cc of water-soluble contrast was
hand injected until resistance was met.

COMPARISON:  ___ CT abdomen pelvis.

FINDINGS: 

Contrast accumulates in the expected location of the gallbladder.  No drainage
into the CBD or intestine is identified. Contrast leak was identified into the
right mid-abdominal peritoneal cavity along the course of the cholecystostomy
tube.  No external contrast leak was identified.

After the exam, the cholecystostomy tube was placed to bag drainage. No
complications during or immediately after this exam.

IMPRESSION: 

Injected contrast does not drain into the CBD or small intestine. Retrograde
contrast leak identified into the right peritoneal cavity along the course of
the cholecystostomy tube becuase of the cystic duct obstruction and the
injection technique.
